# Book of Giants Fragment 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4Q203 frag. 9 (Cave 4) | **Condition:** very fragmentary; destruction narrative partially legible

---

**11:1** [...] then the-holy-ones [...] the-angels-of the-presence [...]

**11:2** [...] received-the-command from-the-Most-High [...]

**11:3** [...] and-they-descended with-fire [...]

**11:4** [...] from-the-throne-of glory [...]

**11:5** [...] and-they-sent fire from-heaven [...]

**11:6** [...] and-it-burned [...] all the-Nephilim [...]

**11:7** [...] and-the-sons-of the-Watchers [...]

**11:8** [...] and-the-earth was-cleansed [...] from-their-pollution [...]

**11:9** [...] and-from-the-blood that-was-shed upon-it [...]

**11:10** [...] and-from-all the-unrighteousness [...]

**11:11** [...] and-the-Watchers were-bound [...] in-chains-of darkness [...]

**11:12** [...] in-the-valleys-of the-earth [...]

**11:13** [...] until the-great-judgment [...]

**11:14** [...] when-they-shall-be-led-away to-the-abyss-of fire [...]

**11:15** [...] to-the-torment and-the-prison of-eternity [...]

---

*EMET notes: Fragment 11 (Angels of Punishment). Source: 4Q203 frag. 9. Aramaic text from Cave 4 Qumran. Hyphenated compounds preserve Aramaic construct-chain syntax and bound morphemes. Square brackets indicate genuine manuscript lacunae where the leather has deteriorated or broken away. The Book of Giants is an Aramaic expansion of the Watcher myth from 1 Enoch 6-16, featuring the Nephilim giants Ohya, Hahya (sons of Shemihazah), Mahaway (son of Baraq'el), and the hero Gilgamesh.*
